findings.text: follow-on: the runs view's compact row gained lane and model_key here, but reckon/crew/query.py is not among the node's declared write paths (plan §7 or the dispatch scope), and scope_probe.py shows the runs view drops and refuses those fields at base; the file the done_when reaches was outside the declared scope, so the plan's write paths for this node are incomplete and should name query.py.

item_verdicts.diff: read the four commits against base bdfb1592; commit 892aa04 adds resolve_name and normalize_identity and wires the readers, 34a38d2 preserves a retired model id's key, fa9f9dc adds the test module, and 5dc28f07 adds the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: fixtures written as claude-opus and as claude with model opus normalise identically (tests/test_old_names_resolve.py:47), all seven legacy aliases are exercised (ALIASES at tests/test_old_names_resolve.py:18), the CLI ledger and the runs view report the pair (tests/test_old_names_resolve.py:137 and :167), the routing-identifier leak check (tests/test_skill_contracts.py:208) is included, and the negative control reddens a fixture; I re-ran the focused gate at head 5dc28f07 in a scratch extraction (reviewer-head-gate.log, 98 passed, EXIT=0) and reproduced the control (reviewer-negative-control.log, 16 failed, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is plan §7, one read-side resolver mapping old backend names, model ids and aliases to a lane-and-model pair; reckon/ledger.py:187 resolve_name and reckon/ledger.py:229 normalize_identity read the catalogue's lanes and aliases tables, and every reader — ledger read_records, run classification, stored reviews, review exclusions and the crew views — calls normalize_identity, so a stored row keeps its own spelling while a reader sees the (lane, model_key) pair.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, four commits, tests line recording two base and two head gate halves with EXIT=0 and the negative control, test_logs naming base.log/head.log/negative-control.log, and baseline_suite and after_suite both present, complete, with zero failures.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/ledger.py, reckon/mcp_views.py, reckon/crew/reports.py, tests/test_old_names_resolve.py and the evidence fragment; git diff --stat bdfb1592 5dc28f07 lists those plus reckon/crew/query.py, which is outside the declared write paths.

justifications.durability: tests/test_old_names_resolve.py:47 asserts resolve_name against literal hardcoded pairs and tests/test_old_names_resolve.py:88 removes one alias and asserts the name stops resolving, both of which redden if the resolver regresses; 19 not 20 — the one softness is that tests/test_old_names_resolve.py:57 derives its expected pair from the same catalogue structure it reads, so a coupled change to both would not be caught.
justifications.evidence: the manifest records complete base and head gate arms each ending EXIT=0 with zero failures and a negative-control log at EXIT=1, and I re-ran the declared focused gate at head 5dc28f07 (reviewer-head-gate.log, 98 passed, EXIT=0) and the alias-removal control (reviewer-negative-control.log, 16 failed, EXIT=1).
justifications.fit: the added names (resolve_name, normalize_identity, _review_backend_excluded, _run_identity_key, _identity_catalogue) state mechanism rather than plan or ticket identity, and the docstrings at reckon/ledger.py:188 and :230 describe the resolution rule with no version, plan or sprint identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:187 resolve_name returns the (lane, model_key) pair for a catalogue alias, lane name, model key, model id or display alias, and reckon/ledger.py:229 normalize_identity applies it at every read site the plan §7 names, so the landed change is exactly the single read-side resolver the goal states.
justifications.reuse: reckon/ledger.py:180 _identity_catalogue reuses flight.read_layer_file and the pre-existing ledger._file_identity rather than adding a second catalogue reader, and a search over reckon/ for an existing name-to-lane resolver found none, so this is the owner the plan §7 calls for and no capability is duplicated.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat bdfb1592 5dc28f07 lists the declared production and test paths plus reckon/crew/query.py, which is not among the plan §7 or dispatch write paths though the runs-view done_when reaches it, and the query.py change is goal-implied rather than gratuitous.
